request: Goal: Make finalize durable and teardown-safe. Scope: Add a journaled lifecycle for merge outcome, finalize metadata, authority deletion, and worktree deletion; exact-target retry after authority deletion; finalize-sync paths that leave the cleanup worktree clean; and teardown-safe logger, dispatcher, post-hook, module-resolution, and filesystem behavior. Out of Scope: Unrelated flow lifecycle changes. Verify fault-injected persistence boundaries converge to an old or new valid state, block cleanup when merge outcome persistence fails, preserve foreign targets, avoid deleted-worktree references, return ok true with exit 0 after cleanup, and centralize flow.json write ownership.

implementationProof.summary: R1: durable typed checkpoints are persisted before every destructive finalize boundary and each invocation retries only the recorded unfinished boundary. R2: cleanup reuses the recorded worktree, branches, commit identity, and binding provenance and rejects stale or foreign targets before deletion. R3: finalize-sync runs, stages, and commits from the retained main repository so it does not dirty the removable worktree. R4: completion uses pre-removal snapshots and the main-repository state owner after worktree removal, including dispatcher and hooks. R5: successful cleanup preserves ok true and exit 0 while warnings remain non-fatal; non-submodule removal failures retain their established recovery code. R6: FinalizeFlowStateOwner is the single main-repository mutation owner for lifecycle, registry, and outbox flow-state writes. R7: the spec-local finalize contract covers every R1-R7 behavior and the focused cleanup suites pass 92/92 without weakening tests.
